author: Scopoli, 1786
status: 나그네새·여름철새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 하천, 자갈밭, 매립지 등 풀이 적고 모래와 자갈이 많은 곳
summary: 전국에 흔히 찾아와 번식하는 여름철새로, 3월 중순에 온다. 하천, 자갈밭, 매립지처럼 풀이 적고 모래와 자갈이 많은 곳에 살며, 종종걸음으로 재빨리 달리다 갑자기 멈춰 곤충을 주로 잡아먹는다. 자갈밭에 둥지를 만들어 알 4개를 낳아 24~25일 동안 품고, 둥지 가까이 침입자가 오면 날개를 늘어뜨리고 소리를 지르며 다친 척하여 포식자를 다른 곳으로 꾀어낸다. 국외에서는 북반구의 온대·아한대·열대와 뉴기니에서 번식하고 아프리카, 인도, 동남아시아에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: short bill with narrow orange base to lower mandible
black markings on lores, crown and ear-coverts

young: 성조 겨울깃과 비슷하지만 몸 윗면에 비늘 무늬가 있고, 머리는 등과 거의 같은 색이며 깃 끝이 연하다. 이마는 흰 바탕에 옅은 황갈색이 섞이고 눈썹선은 거의 보이지 않는다.

art.subject: Little Ringed Plover (Charadrius dubius), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean riverbeds from March to August: forehead white; a black bar across the forecrown, bordered behind by a thin white line before the brown crown; black lores and ear-coverts forming a mask; white throat and white collar around the hindneck; complete black breast band; rest of the underparts white. Upperparts plain grey-brown. Bill short and black, with a narrow orange area at the base of the lower mandible. Conspicuous bright yellow eye-ring around a dark eye. Legs dull pinkish to yellowish.
art.pose: running in short bursts across gravel, then stopping abruptly to pick up an insect
art.scene: Korean summer riverbed: open gravel and sand bar with sparse vegetation; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view standing on gravel: bright yellow eye-ring, black forecrown bar with a white line behind it, black lores and ear-coverts, complete black breast band, white collar, short black bill with orange base below, pinkish legs
adult female, head detail in side view: blackish-brown lores and ear-coverts, slightly narrower yellow eye-ring, blackish-brown forecrown bar, white forehead

juvenile (July–September), side view standing: scaly grey-brown upperparts with pale fringes, head nearly the same colour as the back, white forehead washed pale buff, supercilium barely visible, brownish breast band, yellow eye-ring
art.build: Small, slim plover, 16cm, a little larger than a sparrow and slimmer than other ringed plovers. Rounded head, short neck, rather elongated body. Bill short and fine, shorter than the head. Legs fairly long and thin, dull pinkish-yellow. In flight the upperwing is plain brown without a clear white wing bar; tail brown with white sides. Runs in quick bursts and stops abruptly to pick up insects, with a slight bob of the head.
avoid: Do not paint an orange bill with a black tip or orange legs — that is Common Ringed Plover (Charadrius hiaticula).
Do not paint a white wing bar in flight.
Do not leave out the yellow eye-ring.
Do not paint a long slender bill or a long tail (Long-billed Plover).
